1	# DevDesk Backlog
2	
3	**Last Updated:** 2026-08-03
4	
5	Open work for DevDesk: known defects, technical debt, and planned features.
6	Replaces the former `todo.md` at the repository root. Items completed there
7	(network topology visualisation, inter-container ping/curl) have been dropped
8	rather than carried over.
9	
10	---
11	
12	## 1. Known defects
13	
14	**Three open**, all in the registry browser and all found while reviewing the
15	design for §3.8 rather than by a test. See [§1.3](#13-open). D1–D11 and D15–D19
16	are fixed; §1.1 records what each was and why the chosen fix was the right one.
17	
18	The five that stayed open longest — D4, D8, D9, D10 and D11 — were parked not
19	because they were hard but because each altered something the user already saw,
20	so they needed a deliberate call rather than a drive-by fix. All five were then
21	decided together and fixed in one pass; see [§1.2](#12-the-five-parked-defects).
22	
23	### 1.1 Fixed
24	
25	**The command line took focus from the render path.** Found in phase 5.
26	`renderHeader` called `a.commandInput.Focus()` whenever `commandMode` was set —
27	a mutation inside `View()`, which Rule 110 makes read-only. A
28	`bubbles/textinput` drops every key it receives while blurred, so the command
29	line only accepted typing because a render happened to have run first. Focus is
30	now taken in `enterCommandMode` and released alongside the existing `Blur()`
31	calls on the way out. In production the ordering held, so nothing was visibly
32	broken; the coupling surfaced the moment a test drove the router without
33	rendering, and the same latent bug would bite anyone reordering the loop.
34	
35	**Two views' help advertised keys that do nothing.** Found while writing the
36	phase 2 tests, not previously recorded.
37	
38	The status view's `GetHelpContent` documented `n` for "Add a new monitor" while
39	the binding has been `ctrl+n` since Rule 111 standardised it, and the `/` filter
40	was missing altogether; the empty-state message told the user to "Press [n]" too.
41	The containers view advertised `S` (shell in a new window) in `GetShortcuts()`
42	without documenting it at all.
43	
44	The workspaces view had it too, found in phase 3: `n` and `Enter` documented
45	where the bindings are `ctrl+n` and `enter`, `/` undocumented, and the same
46	stale "Press [n]" in its empty state.
47	
48	`explorer` made it four in a row, though only just: every key was documented
49	except `/`. The check caught it on its first run.
50	
51	`security` broke the streak — its help documents every key its header
52	advertises, across all four states.
53	
54	`oci_resources` then produced the worst instance, in phase 4. The Networks and
55	Volumes tabs documented `n` for a binding that has been `ctrl+n` since Rule 111
56	renamed it — the same drift `status` and `workspaces` carried — but the **whole
57	Registries tab was undocumented**: `ctrl+n`, `e`, `l` and `L` appeared nowhere,
58	so four actions on a tab were reachable only by guessing.
59	
60	That view needed one adjustment to the check: its help qualifies most keys with
61	the tab they belong to (`enter (Images)`, `ctrl+n (Networks)`), so the
62	parenthetical comes off before matching. That convention is worth keeping — with
63	four tabs sharing a keymap, an unqualified `enter` would be ambiguous.
64	
65	So the pattern across five views: the drift is a Rule 111 rename the help did
66	not follow, plus whole surfaces added later and never documented at all.
67	
68	All five are fixed, and every view in `internal/ui` now asserts that each key
69	`GetShortcuts()` advertises appears in `GetHelpContent()` — the check that would
70	have caught the drift when it was introduced.
71	
72	**The explorer acted on a different row than the one highlighted.** Found in
73	phase 3, and the most serious defect the coverage work has turned up.
74	
75	`handleKeyMsg` resolved the cursor against `sortedItems(currentItems())` — the
76	unfiltered list — while the table was built from the filtered one. With a filter
77	active the two indices disagree, so `ctrl+d`, `p`, `→` and `ctrl+w` all acted on
78	whatever happened to sit at that index in the *unfiltered* list. Filtering to a
79	single project and pressing `ctrl+d` scheduled a different group for deletion.
80	`GetShortcuts` had it too, so even the advertised `ctrl+w` keyed off the wrong
81	node.
82	
83	Both now go through `visibleItems()`, the single list `updateTableRows` builds
84	from. Pinned by `TestActionsResolveTheRowTheUserCanSee`, which filters to a row
85	that sits at a different index in each list — the fixtures were chosen so the
86	two cannot coincide.
87	
88	**A stranded cursor in the workspaces table.** `bubbles/table.SetRows` does not
89	clamp the cursor when the row count shrinks. Drilling into a directory with
90	fewer entries — or narrowing the filter — left the cursor past the end: nothing
91	highlighted, and `enter`, `ctrl+d`, `r` and `ctrl+s` all silently did nothing
92	until the user pressed an arrow key. `updateTableData` now clamps.
93	
94	The containers view avoids this by calling `GotoTop()` after every filter
95	change; workspaces had no equivalent. **`explorer` had it too**, and only on the
96	filter path — its drill-down was already safe because it calls `GotoTop()`.
97	Fixed the same way.
98	
99	**Two tabs reported nothing when Docker was down.** Found in phase 4.
100	`handleImagesList` has always set a footer message on failure;
101	`handleNetworksList` and `handleVolumesList` only logged, so with the daemon
102	stopped those two tabs showed an empty table — indistinguishable from "you have
103	no networks". Both now match their sibling.
104	
105	**The Registries tab opened empty.** `switchTab` focused the table and fired the
106	`docker login` status check, but never called `updateRegistryTable()` — so the
107	tab stayed blank until an asynchronous Docker call answered, even though the
108	registries come from the config file and were available immediately.
109	
110	**A search counter with no floor.** `RegistryBrowser.AddRegistryTags`
111	decremented `pendingSearches` unconditionally. A duplicate or late response drove
112	it negative, and the *next* search then started from that base: `IsSearching()`
113	stayed false while requests were genuinely in flight, so the spinner never
114	showed. Floored at zero.
115	
116	**Footer messages with no timer.** `explorer.handleDeleteComplete` set
117	`footerError` and returned `nil`, so a failed delete left "Delete failed — check
118	logs" on screen until something else overwrote it. Rule 128 caps footer messages
119	at three seconds, and the same file's `BrowserOpenedMsg` handler already did it
120	correctly. Now returns `clearFooterErrorCmd()`.
121	
122	The security view had it worse: **Rule 128 was not honoured anywhere in it.**
123	`statusMessage` was set in three places — "Added x to .gitleaksignore", "Failed
124	to ignore secret", "No references available" — and there was no clear timer in
125	the package at all, so whichever happened last stayed on screen until a tab
126	switch happened to reset it. `clearStatusCmd` / `clearStatusMsg` added and all
127	three wired, pinned by `TestFooterMessagesExpire`.
128	
129	**D7** (`extractTarGz` kept parent references in archive paths), **D2** (the
130	"permanent delete" checkbox was documented as locked but was not) and **D5** (an
131	unreachable focus clamp in `CreationForm`) were fixed together — three small,
132	independent defects with no shared code.
133	
134	`extractTarGz` now routes every member name through `sanitizeArchivePath`, which
135	normalises the separators and rejects anything resolving outside the root.
136	Cleaning happens *after* the leading separator is stripped, not before:
137	`path.Clean("/../x")` returns `"/x"`, which would have absorbed the traversal
138	silently instead of exposing it. Traversal that resolves back inside the root
139	(`templates/../README.md`) is kept, normalised. Backslashes are folded to `/`
140	first, so `..\..\etc\passwd` cannot pass as an ordinary filename on a tar reader
141	that treats it as one.
142	
143	The delete modal carries a `locked` flag, set only by
144	`NewDeleteConfirmModalPermanent`. Rather than merely making the toggle a no-op,
145	navigation skips the checkbox entirely (`minFocus()` / `cycleFocus()`) and the
146	line renders dimmed: a focusable control that ignores every key is more
147	confusing than one that is plainly not there.
148	
149	The `CreationForm` clamp was deleted and replaced by a comment recording why it
150	cannot fire, so it is not reintroduced defensively. A test pins the invariant it
151	was guarding.
152	
153	Both self-annulling tests became real assertions:
154	`TestDeleteConfirmModalPermanentCheckboxIsStillToggleable` →
155	`TestDeleteConfirmModalPermanentCheckboxIsLocked` (plus navigation and
156	confirmation cases), and `TestExtractTarGzPreservesParentTraversalInKeys` →
157	`TestExtractTarGzRejectsParentTraversal` (table-driven over five escape shapes)
158	alongside `TestExtractTarGzNormalisesContainedTraversal`.
159	
160	**D1** (`ReportModal.View()` emitted invalid UTF-8), **D3** (`wrapInputLines`
161	looped forever when `wrapWidth <= 0`) and **D6** (`wordWrap` measured bytes) were
162	fixed together, since D1 and D6 were the same byte-vs-rune defect.
163	
164	Rather than patch each call site, the truncation logic moved into
165	`internal/ui/theme/text.go` per Rule 117: `StringWidth`, `TruncateWidth` (keeps
166	the head) and `TruncateTailWidth` (keeps the tail, for paths). All three measure
167	terminal columns, so double-width glyphs are handled too, not just multibyte
168	ones.
169	
170	A **fourth site carried the same defect** and was not recorded here: `truncate`
171	in `internal/ui/security/model.go` sliced bytes exactly like D1 and rendered
172	Trivy finding titles. It is now `theme.TruncateWidth` and the local helper is
173	gone.
174	
175	A **sixth site** closed the family out, in the last package of phase 3:
176	`parseVersion` in `internal/ui/security` truncated its fallback with
177	`result[:15]`. Version strings are ASCII in practice, so this was the
178	lowest-risk of the six — but it is the same pattern, and it is now
179	`theme.TruncateWidth`. Grepping for `[:` on strings across `internal/ui` now
180	returns nothing but slice indexing.
181	
182	The same function had a second defect: it scanned for the version number by
183	taking the first whitespace-separated token starting with `v`, so
184	`gitleaks version 8.18.2` reported its version as **"version"**. A leading `v`
185	now only counts when a digit follows it.
186	
187	A **fifth site** turned up during the phase 3 tests: `firstOutputLine` in
188	`internal/ui/netdiag` sliced `line[:maxLen-3]` to fill the Output column of the
189	results table, so any diagnostic whose first line contained a multibyte rune
190	could be cut in half and bleed across the rows below (Rule 122). Now
191	`theme.TruncateWidth`, pinned by `TestFirstOutputLineKeepsMultibyteRunesIntact`.
192	Worth grepping for `[:` on strings when the remaining phases land.
193	
194	The two pinned tests that `t.Skip()`d became real assertions
195	(`TestReportModalViewKeepsMultibyteRunesIntact`,
196	`TestWordWrapMeasuresColumnsNotBytes`).
197	
198	One call site was deliberately left alone: `truncateResultLine` in
199	`internal/ui/oci_resources/connectivity_form.go` counts runes rather than bytes,
200	so it is correct — merely imprecise on double-width glyphs. Folding it into the
201	theme helpers is a cleanup, not a defect fix.
202	
203	**Every scan came back empty.** Introduced by the `internal/scan` split itself
204	and caught within the hour by the coverage pass that followed it — the clearest
205	argument yet for the surface → split → cover order.
206	
207	Extracting the subprocess seam collapsed two statements into one return:
208	
209	```go
210	return stdout.Bytes(), waitErr(tc.Name, cmd.Wait(), stderr.String())
211	```
212	
213	Operands are evaluated before the call, so `stdout.Bytes()` snapshots the buffer
214	**before** `cmd.Wait()` runs — and `os/exec` fills that buffer from goroutines
215	only Wait is guaranteed to have finished. `Bytes()` returns a slice header with
216	the length at that moment, so later writes are invisible: the report was always
217	empty, every scan reported no findings, and the exit code alone survived. The
218	code it replaced got this right by accident of being written as separate
219	statements.
220	
221	The read now lives in `finish`, after Wait, with the reasoning recorded next to
222	it so it is not re-collapsed. Pinned by `TestTheReportOnStdoutIsWhatComesBack`,
223	which is the test that failed first when the seam was finally exercised.
224	
225	Worth stating plainly: this is the one defect in this list that the tests
226	*introduced* rather than merely found, and it never reached a commit. A
227	mechanical-looking refactor changed evaluation order, which is exactly what a
228	package with no tests under it cannot tell you.
229	
230	**Context isolation in `GitCredentialStorage` never worked.** Found while
231	planning the coverage work, not previously recorded.
232	
233	The three methods carried the DevDesk context in the `path` field of the git
234	credential protocol (`path=devdesk/context/<name>`). Git discards that field
235	unless `credential.useHttpPath` is set, which is off by default, so every
236	credential was keyed on `protocol://host` alone. Two contexts pointing at the
237	same GitLab host silently overwrote each other, and the last one to authenticate
238	won for all of them. Verified against a real `git credential` store before and
239	after the fix; it affects every helper (GCM, wincred, osxkeychain), since git
240	strips the path before the helper is ever called.
241	
242	**Fix:** pass `-c credential.useHttpPath=true` on each invocation. Scoping it to
243	the call leaves the user's git configuration alone — setting it globally would
244	change credential resolution for every repository on the machine. Pinned by
245	`TestGitCredentialIsolatesContexts`.
246	
247	Existing users must re-authenticate: credentials saved under the old
248	path-stripped key no longer match. Those credentials were ambiguous across
249	contexts anyway.
250	
251	Two smaller defects went with it:
252	
253	- `Delete` had no timeout, while `Save` and `Load` bounded themselves to 2 s
254	  precisely so an unconfigured helper could not freeze the TUI. Logout could
255	  hang indefinitely.
256	- The timeout killed only the direct `git` child, though its comment claimed
257	  otherwise. The helper git spawns survives and holds the output pipes open, so
258	  `Run` kept blocking. All three calls now share one `runCredential` helper built
259	  on `exec.CommandContext` plus `WaitDelay`, which bounds the wait on those pipes.
260	
261	`internal/credentials/helper.go` (`HelperStorage`, 137 lines) was deleted rather
262	than fixed: nothing outside its own tests constructed it. It was also broken —
263	`detectHelper()` returns whatever `git config credential.helper` holds, so a
264	common value like `store --file=/path` became the single unfindable command
265	`credential-store --file=/path` — and it hardcoded `protocol=https`, unlike
266	`GitCredentialStorage`, which reads the scheme from the URL.
267	
268	**D15 — `esc` never reached a view that was not editing.** The router answered
269	`esc` itself through `maybeQuitCommandMode`, forwarding it only when the view
270	reported `InEditMode()`. Every esc-to-go-back handler behind that gate was dead
271	code: the explorer's `esc` → `handleDrillUp` could not fire, though Rule 111
272	lists `esc` as the third way up.
273	
274	**Fix:** the router no longer names `esc` at all — it falls through to the
275	default branch and is forwarded like any other key. What made this smaller than
276	it looked is that the router had nothing left to do with `esc` by the time the
277	branch ran: `handleCommandMode` answers first whenever the command line is open,
278	so `maybeQuitCommandMode` was resetting an already-closed line and asking for a
279	redundant resize. It is deleted.
280	
281	The interesting half is what the gate had done to the views. Two of them
282	declared themselves *editing* in states holding no field at all, for one reason
283	— it was the only way to be handed `esc`. The security view said so outright:
284	`InEditMode()` was documented as *"returns true when the view needs to handle
285	ESC key"*, and claimed `StateScanning`, `StateResults` and `StateDetails`;
286	netdiag claimed `StateRunning` and `StateDetails`. That claim costs more than it
287	buys, because `InEditMode()` also governs `:`, `q` and `?` — so the security
288	results screen, the one place a user most wants to jump elsewhere, was the one
289	place `:` did nothing. Both predicates are now about focus and nothing else, and
290	those states get the command line, the help overlay and quit back.
291	
292	Left alone deliberately: the containers view claims `stateLogs`, where `q`
293	really is the view's own key for leaving the log pane. That is key ownership,
294	not a workaround for `esc`.
295	
296	**D16 — `:netdiag` was documented but not accepted.** One missing map entry.
297	**D17 — the completion catalogue was a subset of the parser.** Eight commands
298	listed against fourteen views plus aliases, kept by hand in two places.
299	
300	**Fix, for both:** one map. `viewNames` in `parser.go` maps every accepted
301	spelling to its view, the key equal to the `ViewType` being the full name and
302	every other key an alias; `GetAliases()` and the new `FullNames()` derive from
303	it, and the completion engine derives from those. Two tests hold the two ends
304	together — everything the parser accepts is suggested, everything suggested
305	parses — so the lists cannot drift apart again. `ParseCommand` lost its chain of
306	`if mainCmd ==` comparisons to the same treatment, `actionNames` and
307	`actionAliases`, and `Parse` is now a lookup in `viewNames` rather than a third
308	copy of it.
309	
310	Two aliases documented in `CLAUDE.md` but accepted nowhere came out of this —
311	`gle` for the explorer and `w` for workspaces — the same defect as D16, found by
312	the test rather than by reading. `ViewNet` was renamed `ViewNetdiag` and its
313	value changed from `net` to `netdiag`, so the full name matches the view, the
314	package and the documentation; `net` remains an alias.
315	
316	**D18 — the header overflowed a narrow window.** `buildShortcutLines` meant to
317	clip the shortcut block to its column — the comment said *"Truncate if wider
318	than col2Width"* — but called `theme.PadWithBg`, which returns content untouched
319	once it is already at or past the target. Below roughly 100 columns the header
320	rendered wider than the window and wrapped, costing the viewport a row.
321	
322	**Fix:** `lipgloss.NewStyle().MaxWidth(col2Width)`, which truncates on rune
323	boundaries without cutting an escape sequence in half — the corruption Rule 122
324	is about. Width 80 is now part of `TestEveryHeaderRowFillsTheWidth`, and a
325	second test checks no row ends inside an escape sequence, which is the failure a
326	naive slice would have produced.
327	
328	### 1.2 The five parked defects
329	
330	D4, D8, D9, D10 and D11 were each recorded rather than fixed on discovery,
331	because each changed something the user already saw. They were decided together
332	and fixed in one pass. Three of the five had a test written to fail *on the
333	fix*, and all three did.
334	
335	**D4 — `tab` navigated the delete confirmation.** Rule 135 reserves `tab` for
336	switching tabs and assigns field navigation to `↑ / ↓` exclusively; the modal
337	had it exactly inverted, cycling on `tab` and clamping on `↑ / ↓`. `↑ / ↓` now
338	cycle, which is what keeps every control reachable in one direction, and the
339	`tab` cases are gone. The explorer no longer advertises "tab Navigate" while the
340	modal is open, and `↑↓` is not advertised in its place — Rule 138 calls it
341	obvious. The permanent variant still skips its locked checkbox, so cycling there
342	toggles between the two buttons.
343	
344	**D8 — write-only CRUD flags.** `creating`, `editing` and `confirming` were
345	assigned in five places and read in none, and `ComponentFormCancelledMsg` — the
346	only thing that would have reset two of them — could never be sent. Deleted, all
347	of it. Nothing else changed: the phase 2 tests had deliberately asserted on
348	`componentForm` / `confirmModal` rather than on the flags, which is what made
349	this safe a phase later.
350	
351	**D9 — the containers list opened Z→A.** `New()` set neither `sortColumn` nor
352	`sortAsc`, so both took their zero value. Both are now set explicitly, so the
353	default is stated rather than inherited. `TestDefaultSortIsNameDescending`
354	became `TestDefaultSortIsNameAscending`, and the cycle test walks forward from
355	ascending. The `loadedModel` helper still sets the sort itself even though it
356	now matches the constructor: those tests should say which order they rely on.
357	
358	**D10 — a registry failure was invisible.** `renderTemplateList` returned early
359	when the field was unfocused and the warning sat below that return, so a form
360	opened after the OCI registry failed offered a Template field reading "none"
361	with nothing to distinguish "the registry is down" from "there are no
362	templates". The warning moved into `renderTemplateWarning` and is appended in
363	both branches — it explains why the list is empty, so it belongs wherever the
364	list is.
365	
366	**D11 — CRITICAL and HIGH rendered identically.** `getSeverityStyle` composed
367	CRITICAL by hand as `ColorError` + `Bold`, which is byte-for-byte the
368	`theme.StatusErrorStyle` it returned for HIGH. The palette moved to
369	`theme.SeverityTextStyle`, next to the `TableStylesForSeverity` it draws from,
370	and the view delegates (Rule 102). An unrecognised severity now falls back to
371	the info colour rather than to `DimStyle`, so it is still legible.
372	
373	The pattern worth keeping: when a defect is recorded rather than fixed, write
374	the test **inverted** — asserting the current behaviour and saying so. D9, D10
375	and D11 each had one, and each failed the moment the fix landed, which is how
376	the stale test and the stale backlog entry got found together.
377	
378	### 1.3 Open
379	
380	D12–D14 sit in `internal/ui/oci_resources` and are cheap on their own, but
381	§3.8 rewrites the code path each of them lives in. Fix them **as part of** that
382	work rather than ahead of it, and write each one's test inverted first, per the
383	pattern above.
384	
385	D15–D19 were found by the phase 5 pass, were unrelated to §3.8, and are fixed —
386	see §1.1. Each had been recorded with an inverted test asserting the broken
387	behaviour; those tests are what failed when the fix landed, and each has been
388	turned around to assert the fixed behaviour instead.
389	
390	**D12 — `AuthEnabled` has no effect on browse or discovery.** The flag is
391	honoured in exactly three places: the `docker login` fired on form submit, the
392	`Logged` column, and the URL list `registryLoginStatusCmd` checks. Neither code
393	path that actually talks to a registry consults it. `submitSearch`
394	(`browser_keys.go:142`) calls `docker.GetStoredCreds(credURL)`
395	unconditionally and hands the result to `searchRegistryTagsCmd`;
396	`detectRegistryGroupCmd` (`commands.go:563`) does the same before calling into
397	`registrymgr`. A registry the user has marked as needing no authentication will
398	still have the host's stored credentials sent to it whenever any other registry
399	on that host has been logged into — which, given that Docker keys credentials by
400	host, is the normal case for a Nexus instance. This is the defect the
401	`anonymous` mode in §3.8 exists to make expressible; today there is no way to
402	say "do not send credentials here" at all.
403	
404	**D13 — the browser cannot be dismissed while it is resolving.**
405	`handleKeyMsg` returns `nil` for every key in `browserStateResolving`
406	(`browser_keys.go:70`), `esc` included, and that state is entered
407	unconditionally on open whenever any registry is configured. The detections run
408	concurrently with an 8 s timeout each, so the wedge is bounded at roughly eight
409	seconds — but it is eight seconds during which the application ignores the user,
410	on a screen they may have opened by mistake. §3.8 removes the state rather than
411	the symptom: with members read from config and cache, there is nothing to
412	resolve and the form renders immediately.
413	
414	A smaller thing in the same handler, not worth its own entry:
415	`HandleGroupDetected` matches the incoming result against `reg.URL`, so two
416	registries configured with the same URL collide and the second result overwrites
417	the first. The slug introduced in §3.8 is the natural key to match on instead.
418	
419	**D14 — the registry filter shows a raw URL for group members.**
420	`registryFilterLabel()` (`browser_tags.go:63`) resolves the active filter by
421	searching `b.registries`, which holds only the configured top-level entries.
422	Discovered members are not in that list, so filtering to one falls through to
423	returning `b.registryFilter` — the full synthesised URL — where every other row
424	in the same view shows a short alias. The fix follows from §3.8 rather than
425	preceding it: once members are persisted they are resolvable, and the filter
426	gains a group level at the same time.
427	
428	---
429	
430	## 2. Technical debt
431	
432	### Test coverage
433	
434	Currently **73.6 %** overall; the agreed target is 80 %.
435	
436	Phased plan, with the harness and most of phase 1 delivered:
437	
438	| Phase | Scope | Status |
439	|---|---|---|
440	| 0 | `internal/ui/testutil` Bubble Tea harness | **done** (100 %) |
441	| 1 | Leaf components and pure helpers | **done** except the `ui/theme` complement (~55 stmts) |
442	| 2 | Mid-size view state machines (`status`, `containers`, `dashboard`, `gitlab/auth`) | **done** |
443	| 3 | Large views (`workspaces`, `explorer`, `security`, `netdiag`) | **done** |
444	| 4 | `ui/oci_resources` | **done** — 43.4 %, the rest deferred to phase 6 |
445	| 5 | Router and I/O seams (`app`, `scan`, `docker`) | **done** — `app` 90.5 %, `scan` 99.2 %, `docker` 65.4 % |
446	| 6 | Remainder to reach 80 % | pending |
447	
448	**Phase 5 is complete.** The three packages needed three different seams, which
449	is the finding worth carrying into phase 6: `app` needed only a constructor that
450	does not read the terminal, `docker` needed `dockerRunner`, and `scan` needed
451	`commandRunner` plus pure argument builders. None of them needed a mocking
452	library.
453	
454	Phase 6 starts from `internal/registrymgr` (18.5 %), `internal/oci` (37.3 %),
455	`internal/ui/oci_resources` (43.4 %, deferred there deliberately),
456	`internal/status` (64.8 %) and `internal/docker` (65.4 %). The last two are the
457	ones that now have a seam under them and no excuse.

734	### Race detector cannot run locally
735	
736	`mise run test-race` needs cgo and therefore a C compiler on `PATH`. Without one
737	it fails with `cgo: C compiler "gcc" not found`. Bubble Tea `Cmd`s run
738	concurrently, so this is the check most likely to catch a Rule 110 violation.
739	
740	**Now covered by CI.** `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs `mise run test-race` on
741	every push and pull request, on `ubuntu-latest`, which has a toolchain. The first
742	run reported no data race across all 17 packages.
743	
744	That is a baseline, not a clean bill of health: the detector only sees code the
745	tests actually execute, and coverage is 73.6 %. Rule 110 violations in untested
746	paths remain invisible. The two efforts compound, so this is an argument for the
747	coverage phases rather than a substitute for them.
748	
749	`internal/scan` is the package the detector has most to say about, since
750	`Scanner.Scan` is the only place in the application that fans out to concurrent
751	goroutines writing one shared result. Its tests now drive all five stages at
752	once, so that fan-out is under the detector for the first time — but only on CI,
753	which is where the confirmation has to be read.

853	#### Model mismatches to settle before coding
854	
855	These are not implementation details; they decide what the abstraction can even
856	promise.
857	
858	- **Nesting — settled.** The explorer is a tree of groups → subgroups →
859	  projects. GitHub has no nested groups, but it does have **organisations**, and
860	  a user can belong to several. Flattening everything to one level was
861	  considered and rejected: someone in five orgs would get a wall of repositories
862	  with no way to tell them apart by owner. The abstraction therefore **declares
863	  its depth** — `MaxDepth: 1` for GitHub (orgs at level 1, repositories at level
864	  2), unbounded for GitLab. This costs nothing in the UI: the drill-down already
865	  handles two levels, and a user with no organisation simply sees a flat list.
866	- **Deletion.** `DeleteGroup` / `DeleteProject` implement GitLab's two-step
867	  permanent delete (schedule, then purge under the renamed
868	  `-deletion_scheduled-<id>` path). GitHub deletes immediately and has no
869	  equivalent, so the "permanent" checkbox is meaningless there. The `locked`
870	  flag added in §1.1 is the hook for that: a GitHub backend would set it and
871	  leave the box out of reach, as the already-scheduled GitLab case does.
872	- **Dashboard counters.** `FetchDashboardStats` reads `X-Total` from five list
873	  endpoints. GitHub has no equivalent header for these; the counts come from the
874	  search API (`search/issues?q=is:open+is:pr+assignee:@me`), with different rate
875	  limits and semantics.
876	- **Vocabulary.** Group/project/merge request vs organisation/repository/pull
877	  request. The UI must pick per-backend labels or a neutral vocabulary; Rule 129
878	  applies either way.
879	
880	#### Settled: vocabulary, commands and forge selection
881	
882	The organising distinction, which the mismatches above blur: the two forges
883	differ in **words** and in **shapes**, and only the first is a presentation
884	problem.
885	
886	| Difference | Kind | Handled by |
887	|---|---|---|
888	| "Group" vs "Organization" | word | vocabulary table |
889	| "Merge Request" vs "Pull Request" | word | vocabulary table |
890	| Token label, placeholder, help URL | word | vocabulary table |
891	| Icon and display name | word | vocabulary table |
892	| Nested namespaces | **shape** | declared depth (above) |
893	| Visibility set — 3 values vs 2 | **shape** | forge-supplied option list |
894	| Role model — int levels vs strings | **shape** | backend returns a humanised role |
895	| Two-step permanent delete | **shape** | the `locked` flag, §1.1 |
896	| Dashboard counters | **shape** | different endpoints, above |
897	
898	Words are cheap and settle in one pass. Shapes are the actual work, and neither
899	neutral nor per-forge wording helps with them. Keeping the two apart is what
900	stops the vocabulary layer from quietly growing conditionals.
901	
902	**Vocabulary is per-forge, not neutral.** A GitLab user says *group*, a GitHub
903	user says *repository*; "namespace" is a third language nobody speaks, and it
904	makes the application read as an abstraction layer rather than a tool. The
905	wording lives in a single `Vocabulary` value per forge — name, icon, namespace
906	singular/plural, repository, change-request, token label and placeholder, help
907	URL, visibility set, role names — resolved once from the active context and
908	carried on `shared.State`, which every view already receives.
909	
910	The rule that keeps it maintainable: **no view interpolates a forge name into a
911	string literal.** That is enforceable the way this project already pins

983	#### Open decision: Go SDKs or the `gh` / `glab` CLIs
984	
985	Worth deciding before any code is written, because it determines whether the
986	package needs a seam.
987	
988	Arguments for the CLIs:
989	
990	- Authentication is already solved, including OAuth device flow, self-hosted
991	  hosts and token storage. DevDesk's own credential handling could shrink — and
992	  it has already proven fragile (see §1.1).
993	- `gh api` and `glab api` are raw REST/GraphQL passthroughs, so no SDK is needed
994	  for coverage of endpoints the abstraction does not model.
995	- No SDK version churn to track for two forges.
996	
997	Arguments against:
998	
999	- **Per-context isolation conflicts with how these tools store auth.** Both keep
1000	  global per-host state (`~/.config/gh/hosts.yml`). DevDesk contexts want
1001	  *different tokens for the same host*. Driving `gh auth switch` from the TUI
1002	  would mutate the user's global CLI state — the exact mistake avoided in §1.1 by
1003	  scoping `credential.useHttpPath` to the invocation. The clean route is
1004	  `GH_TOKEN` / `GITLAB_TOKEN` per invocation, but then DevDesk still owns the
1005	  tokens and the main benefit is gone.
1006	- **Two more hard dependencies.** Today DevDesk needs `git`, and `docker` only
1007	  for the features that use it. Requiring `gh` and `glab` for the core forge
1008	  feature is a real setup-friction regression.
1009	- **Cost per call.** A process spawn per request, against a reused HTTP
1010	  connection today. The dashboard alone issues five calls, and the explorer
1011	  paginates.
1012	- **Testability regresses.** `internal/gitlab` reaches 100 % with no seam,
1013	  because the SDK takes a base URL that an `httptest` server can stand in for.
1014	  Shelling out would put it back in the position `internal/docker` was in, needing
1015	  a manufactured seam — and stubbed CLI output encodes assumptions about the tool
1016	  rather than testing against it.
1017	
1018	**Current recommendation:** keep Go SDKs (go-gitlab, go-github) for the API
1019	surface, and use the CLIs only as an *optional* token source — when a context has
1020	no token, offer to read one from `gh auth token --hostname <host>` or
1021	`glab auth status`. That takes the convenience without the coupling. Recorded as
1022	a recommendation, not a decision.

1052	### 3.7 Command mode from inside a text field — **done**
1053	
1054	`alt+:` now opens the command line from anywhere, including a focused text
1055	input. A bare `:` keeps its old, conditional behaviour, so muscle memory
1056	survives.
1057	
1058	The problem: `handleKeyMsg` routed `:` through `maybeEnterInCommandMode`, which
1059	asked the view whether it was in edit mode (`FormView.InEditMode()`) and, if it
1060	was, forwarded the keystroke to the active input. Command mode was therefore
1061	unreachable from any form, filter box or search field — most of the application.
1062	
1063	The security view is the case that settles it. `InEditMode()` is true there for
1064	the target path, Trivy server and Gitleaks config fields, and the Trivy server
1065	placeholder is `https://trivy-server:4954` — the field has to accept **two**
1066	colons to hold a valid value. Forwarding `:` to the input is not a bug; it is
1067	the only correct behaviour, which is precisely why `:` cannot be the
1068	authoritative key. The only way in was to move focus to a control that takes no
1069	text and press `:` there, so reachability depended on which widget was focused
1070	and nothing said so.
1071	
1072	It was worse in `StateScanning`, `StateResults`, `StateDetails` and while a
1073	confirm modal is open: `InEditMode()` is true and there is no field to move
1074	focus to. `:` was forwarded to the view, which has no `case` for it — no view in
1075	the application handles `:` itself — and dropped silently.
1076	
1077	#### Why `alt+`, not `ctrl+`
1078	
1079	`ctrl+:` cannot be made to work, and this is the note that should stop anyone
1080	reintroducing it. A terminal encodes Ctrl by clearing bits, which only covers
1081	ASCII `@` through `_` (0x40–0x5F). `:` is 0x3A: Ctrl+: sends a plain `:` or
1082	nothing. Reporting it as a distinct key needs the Kitty keyboard protocol or
1083	xterm's `modifyOtherKeys`, and bubbletea v1.3.10 implements neither. A
1084	`case "ctrl+:"` would be dead code.
1085	
1086	Alt has no such limit — a terminal sends ESC then the key, and bubbletea reports
1087	that as the key carrying `Alt`. The alternative considered was a free
1088	`ctrl+<letter>` (`b g l p t u v x z` are unused; `ctrl+i m j h [` are Tab, Enter,
1089	LF, Backspace and Esc and must be left alone), which is marginally more portable
1090	but loses the `:` in the gesture.
1091

1119	### 3.8 Docker registry groups
1120	
1121	Two shapes have to be supported: a remote registry with or without
1122	authentication, and a **group** fronting several remote registries, itself
1123	reachable anonymously or not. The second is the one the current model cannot
1124	express.
1125	
1126	Not started. The decisions below are settled; one is not, and is marked as such.
1127	
1128	#### What the current code does
1129	
1130	| Concern | Today | Where |
1131	|---|---|---|
1132	| Parent/child relation | in memory only, for the lifetime of one browser session | `registry_browser.go:26` (`browserRegistryEntry`) |
1133	| Group discovery | Nexus REST, re-run on **every** browser open, 8 s timeout each, behind a blocking spinner | `registry_browser.go:153`, `registrymgr/nexus.go` |
1134	| Member URLs | synthesised as `host + /repository/<memberName>`, alias stripped of `-proxy`/`-hosted`/`-local` | `nexus.go:111`, `nexus.go:200` |
1135	| Credential inheritance | member searches use the **parent's** URL as the `~/.docker/config.json` lookup key | `browser_keys.go:130` |
1136	| Registries tab | flat table, no indication a group was ever found | `table.go:182` |
1137	| Result filter (`r`) | cycles member URLs; no group level | `browser_tags.go:25` |
1138	
1139	`RegistryConfig.Registries` is a flat `[]RegistryItem` and carries no parent
1140	field. Nothing about a group survives closing the browser: it is rediscovered,
1141	over the network, next time.
1142	
1143	The credential inheritance is the one piece that already behaves correctly, and
1144	the reason it does is the same reason the open decision below is hard.
1145	
1146	#### Settled
1147	
1148	| Ref | Decision |
1149	|---|---|
1150	| A | **One list, one discriminator, one parent pointer** — `kind: registry \| group` plus `parent` on `RegistryItem`. Two parallel lists and a recursive `Children` tree were both rejected. |
1151	| 1 | The parent is referenced by **slug**, not by URL. |
1152	| 3 | Discovered members live in a **disk cache**, not in `config.yaml`. |
1153	| 4 | The Registries tab gets **drill-down** navigation (`←` / `→`), not an indented tree and not a `Group` column. |
1154	| 5 | **No purely logical groups.** A group always corresponds to a real repository-manager group. |
1155	| F | `provider` is a **declared field**, not sniffed from the URL. |
1156	
1157	**A — one list.** A Nexus group *is* a pullable registry as well as a container,
1158	so splitting `registries` and `registry_groups` would have duplicated the form,
1159	the table and the credential handling to model a distinction the server does not
1160	make. A single list with a discriminator keeps one table, one form (fields shown
1161	per `kind`), and leaves sorting and filtering intact.
1162	
1163	**1 — slug over URL.** The URL is today's de facto identifier and is threaded
1164	through `registryLoginStatus`, the scan cache keys and the message types, which
1165	is exactly why it is the wrong thing to hang a parent link on: editing a group's
1166	URL would silently orphan its members. The slug replaces the URL **only as the
1167	parent link and the cache key** — everything Docker-facing stays keyed on the
1168	URL, because that is what Docker itself is keyed on. Existing configs migrate by
1169	deriving a slug from the alias, falling back to the URL host; uniqueness has to
1170	be enforced at load, and the form needs to reject a collision rather than accept
1171	a config that will not round-trip.
1172	
1173	**3 — cache, not config.** Discovered members are derived data with a server as
1174	their source of truth, and `config.yaml` is what the user declares. Putting them
1175	in the cache mirrors `ImageScanCache` and `WorkspaceScanCache` (Rule 126) rather
1176	than inventing a fourth persistence shape:
1177	`~/.devdesk/cache/registry-groups.json`, keyed by group slug, refreshed
1178	explicitly with `ctrl+r` on a group row. The browser then reads config plus
1179	cache and opens instantly and offline, which is what removes D13's blocking
1180	state rather than papering over it. A `Members` column showing the count and
1181	`theme.TimeAgo(discovered_at)` (Rule 127) is what keeps staleness visible —
1182	without it, a silently stale cache is worse than the current re-detection.
1183	
1184	**4 — drill-down.** Level 1 lists groups and standalone registries; `→` enters a
1185	group and lists its members; `←` goes back, with a breadcrumb below the table
1186	(Rules 111, 123). The indented-tree alternative reads faster at five registries
1187	but breaks the moment the table is sorted or the FilterBar (Rule 136) narrows
1188	it, and drill-down is already the pattern `gitlab-explorer` uses. Proposed
1189	columns: `Alias | URL | Kind | Auth | Login | Members`.
1190	
1191	**5 — no logical groups.** Grouping unrelated registries under a user-invented
1192	name was considered and dropped: it has no server to discover from, no shared
1193	credential to inherit, and no group URL to pull through, so it would be a
1194	display-only concept carrying the weight of a real one. If the need for
1195	arbitrary grouping appears later it is a saved-selection feature in the browser,
1196	not a change to the registry model.
1197	
1198	**F — declared provider.** `NexusDetector.CanHandle` currently returns true
1199	whenever `ManagementURL` is non-empty (`nexus.go:31`), which makes that field do
1200	double duty as an implicit "this is Nexus" flag and makes the detector list
1201	effectively single-vendor. A `provider` field on the group — `nexus`, `harbor`,
1202	`artifactory`, `gitlab`, `generic` — turns `CanHandle` into a match on a
1203	declared value, with the generic detector last. It is a cycle field in the form
1204	(Rule 132) and it is what makes a second implementation possible without
1205	guessing.

1207	#### Open: how far credential inheritance goes
1208	
1209	The concrete case: a Nexus group **with** authentication fronting eight Nexus
1210	proxies. Browsing the proxy that points at `dhi.io` has to query the *proxy's*
1211	URL while authenticating with the *group's* credentials.
1212	
1213	That much the code already does — `submitSearch` sets
1214	`credURL = parentURL ?: entry.URL` — and the reason it works is worth stating
1215	explicitly, because it constrains everything else:
1216	
1217	> **`docker login` takes a registry host, not a path.** `~/.docker/config.json`
1218	> is keyed on `host[:port]`, so the group and all eight proxies share one single
1219	> credential entry, because they share `nexus.example.com`.
1220	
1221	Three consequences:
1222	
1223	- `inherit` is not a convenience for path-based groups, it is the **only** thing
1224	  the credential store can represent. Every member of such a group authenticates
1225	  identically whether the model says so or not.
1226	- A per-member `credentials` override is **not storable today**. It would need a
1227	  secret keyed by slug rather than by registry URL, which `docker login` cannot
1228	  represent.
1229	
1230	  §3.9 changes what this costs, without changing the conclusion. DevDesk now has
1231	  a store — the host's, keyed by whatever string it likes — so a slug-keyed
1232	  password is no longer unstorable in principle, and it would not put plaintext
1233	  anywhere. What it would still do is take DevDesk out of `docker login`'s model
1234	  and into maintaining its own registry auth, for a case (§3.8) that has not been
1235	  shown to exist. `RegistryItem` still has no password field by construction, and
1236	  that is still the right default.
1237	- What a member *can* usefully override is **`anonymous`**: do not send the
1238	  group's credentials to this one. That is representable, costs nothing, and is
1239	  the safety valve — and it is the same mechanism D12 needs.
1240	
1241	Proposed, pending the discussion: replace `AuthEnabled bool` with an `AuthMode`
1242	cycle field where a group is `anonymous | credentials` and a member is
1243	`inherit | anonymous`. The four cases in scope then map cleanly:
1244	
1245	| Case | Group | Member |
1246	|---|---|---|
1247	| Remote registry, no auth | — | `kind: registry`, `anonymous` |
1248	| Remote registry, auth | — | `kind: registry`, `credentials` |
1249	| Group with auth, 8 proxies (the case above) | `credentials` | `inherit` |
1250	| Anonymous group | `anonymous` | `inherit` |
1251	
1252	What still needs deciding is whether a member-level `credentials` is worth
1253	supporting at all. It only becomes meaningful for a group whose members are on
1254	different hosts, which decision 5 has just ruled out of the model — so the
1255	current reading is that it should not exist, and that a genuine need for it is a
1256	separate decision about who stores the password.
1257	
1258	**Adjacent question to settle before the model is frozen: browse and pull may
1259	not share a URL.** Path-based Nexus access answers the registry API at
1260	`/repository/<name>/v2/...`, which is what `registryAPIURL` builds and what the
1261	tag search relies on. Whether `docker pull` accepts the same path-form reference
1262	depends on the deployment — a dedicated HTTP connector port per repository is
1263	the older Nexus arrangement, path routing needs a reverse proxy in front. If
1264	they differ, a member needs a third URL alongside `url` and `management_url`,
1265	and `multiImageName` (`browser_tags.go:125`) is building an unpullable
1266	reference today. **This should be checked against the actual Nexus instance**
1267	rather than reasoned about; it is one `docker pull` away from being answered.

1300	### 3.9 Every secret goes to a host secret manager, and radio buttons go away — **done**
1301	
1302	No secret DevDesk holds is written to a file DevDesk owns. Tokens and registry
1303	passwords go to the Windows Credential Manager, the macOS Keychain or a Secret
1304	Service implementation on Linux, through one storage and one only.
1305	
1306	#### What was wrong
1307	
1308	Three of the five storage paths were plaintext on disk, and the option the UI
1309	labelled "secure" was one of them.
1310	
1311	| Secret | Destination | Protection |
1312	|---|---|---|
1313	| Forge token | `~/.devdesk/credentials-<ctx>.json` | **plaintext JSON**, 0600 |
1314	| Forge token | `gitlab.token` in `contexts/<ctx>/config.yaml` | **plaintext YAML** |
1315	| Forge token | git credential helper | whatever the helper does |
1316	| Registry password | `~/.docker/config.json` via `docker login` | whatever Docker's `credsStore` does |
1317	| Registry password | `registry.password` in `config.yaml` | **plaintext YAML**, read at `explorer/create.go:43,132` |
1318	
1319	`ChainStorage.Save` wrote to **every** storage in the chain, and all three
1320	construction sites built it as `NewChainStorage(FileStorage,
1321	GitCredentialStorage)`. Choosing **"Save to Git Credential Manager (secure)"**
1322	therefore stored the token in the credential manager *and* in
1323	`~/.devdesk/credentials-<context>.json` in plaintext. Reads made it worse:
1324	`FileStorage` was first and `ChainStorage.Load` returned the first hit, so the
1325	plaintext file was authoritative and the credential manager was never consulted
1326	while it existed. The secure backend was decorative in both directions.
1327	
1328	The other option was no better in a different way: **"Save token to config file
1329	(less secure)"** set `saveToHelper = false`, so nothing reached the chain and
1330	the token landed only in `config.yaml`. Both options put the token in plaintext;
1331	the "secure" one did it twice.
1332	
1333	And logout did not clean up: `handleLogoutComplete` cleared
1334	`m.config.GitLab.Token` in memory with no `config.Save` behind it, so the token
1335	survived in `contexts/<ctx>/config.yaml`.
1336	
1337	#### The distinction that decided the design
1338	
1339	Delegating to `git credential` delegates to **whatever helper git happens to be
1340	configured with**. If that is `store`, the token lands in `~/.git-credentials`
1341	in plaintext — the same failure, relocated. Only `manager` (GCM),
1342	`osxkeychain`, `libsecret` and `wincred` reach a real OS store. "Goes through
1343	git credential" is not the same claim as "encrypted at rest", and the
1344	requirement was the second one.
1345	
1346	So the host store is the primary path and git credential is kept as an explicit
1347	alternative, for users who want their tokens where GCM already puts everything
1348	else. Only the first can promise what the requirement asks; the second is the
1349	pragmatic option and stays reachable without becoming the default.
1350	
1351	#### What shipped
1352	
1353	**`KeyringStorage` over `zalando/go-keyring`** (`credentials/keyring.go`), one
1354	implementation covering all three platforms with no cgo: wincred on Windows, the
1355	`security` binary on macOS, D-Bus Secret Service elsewhere. Entries are filed
1356	under service `devdesk`, account `<context>/<url>`, so two contexts pointing at
1357	the same host keep separate secrets — the property `GitCredentialStorage` needed
1358	`credential.useHttpPath` to get (§1.1).
1359	
1360	`KeyringAvailable()` probes with a **read** of an account that is never written.
1361	A miss proves the backend answered and simply holds nothing; anything else is
1362	the backend being absent. It runs on every launch, including on machines where
1363	the store turns out to be unusable, so it must not be able to leave anything
1364	behind.
1365	
1366	**`Select(context, preference)`** (`credentials/select.go`) returns a
1367	`Selection{Storage, Backend, Detail}` and picks exactly one destination — host
1368	store, else git credential, else memory. Writing to several at once is what
1369	produced the defect above, so the chain is gone rather than reordered.
1370	`app.secret_backend` pins the head of that list (`auto`, `keyring`,
1371	`git-credential`). A pinned backend that turns out to be unreachable falls
1372	through to memory rather than silently to the other one: someone who asked for
1373	the keyring should not be handed a git helper without being told.
1374	
1375	`gitHelperUsable()` refuses `store` by name and refuses an unset helper, and
1376	accepts everything else. There is no list of good helpers to check against —
1377	enumerating them would only mean rejecting the next one someone installs.
1378	
1379	**The fallback is worse on purpose.** With no store reachable the answer is
1380	`MemoryStorage` — session-only, re-authenticate each launch — and the auth view
1381	says so in `ColorWarn`. That is deliberately worse UX than a file, and that is
1382	the point: a fallback that is silently insecure is how the "secure" option came
1383	to exist.
1384	
1385	**`FileStorage` and `ChainStorage` are deleted.** `MemoryStorage` gained a mutex:
1386	it is now one instance shared by the Cmd goroutines of every view, which the
1387	per-call construction it used to get had hidden.
1388	
1389	**`GitLabConfig.Token` and `RegistryConfig.Password` are out of the schema.**
1390	Parsing and ignoring them would have left the secret on disk forever for every
1391	existing user, so `MigrateLegacySecrets` runs on load and on every context
1392	switch: it reads the two fields straight from the YAML —
1393	`config.ReadLegacySecrets` — moves them into the store, and deletes them from
1394	the file. The rewrite edits the parsed YAML tree rather than round-tripping
1395	through `Config`, which would rewrite every key including the defaults
1396	`applyDefaults` filled in. A secret the store refused to take stays in the file;
1397	losing it would be worse than leaving it. A secret with no URL has no key to be
1398	filed under and no host it could be used against, so it is dropped — and the
1399	auth view reports every one of these outcomes in words.
1400	
1401	`Auth.Authenticate(url, token)` lost its `saveCredentials` parameter and always
1402	stores; `AuthenticateOnly` is the auto-login path, whose token already came out
1403	of the store. Logout deletes from the store, and there is no longer a config
1404	copy to forget about — which is what closes the last defect above.
1405	
1406	`registry.password` had no UI to set it and one reader, `explorer/create.go`.
1407	That reader now asks the store, keyed by the registry URL, and treats a miss as
1408	"anonymous registry" — which is the common case.
1409	
1410	**The radios are gone**, with `SaveToHelper` / `SaveToConfig`, the `saveOption`
1411	field, `theme.RenderRadioButton` (its only two call sites), and the `ctrl+s` /
1412	`ctrl+f` shortcuts and their help section. The form went from five fields to
1413	three, now named `fieldURL` / `fieldToken` / `fieldSubmit` instead of the
1414	integers 0–4. Removing the `case " "` had a side effect worth recording: space
1415	could not previously be typed into the URL or token field, because the radio
1416	handler swallowed it before the input saw it.
1417	
1418	Rules 120 and 132 in `.claude/rules/tui-forms.md` now say cycle fields are the
1419	only control for a closed set, whatever its size, and that checkboxes remain for
1420	independent booleans.
1421	
1422	#### What a user has to do
1423	
1424	Nothing, on any platform. The migration is automatic and the auth view reports
1425	what it did. Two consequences are worth knowing:
1426	
1427	- On a headless Linux box with no D-Bus session and no git helper, DevDesk now
1428	  asks for the token on each launch instead of reading it from a plaintext file.
1429	  That is the intended trade, and it is stated on screen rather than inferred.
1430	- The entry is visible in the host's own UI (`Credential Manager`, `Keychain
1431	  Access`, `seahorse`) under `devdesk`, which is where a user should be able to
1432	  revoke it.
1433	
1434	#### One rough edge, left rough on purpose
1435	
1436	On Linux, `go-keyring` calls `Unlock` on the login collection before every read,
1437	including the availability probe. On a desktop whose keyring unlocks with the
1438	session password — the default on GNOME and KDE — that returns immediately. On
1439	one configured with a separately-locked keyring, it raises the agent's unlock
1440	prompt at startup, before the TUI has drawn its first frame, and blocks until it
1441	is answered.
1442	
1443	Wrapping the probe in a timeout would make this worse, not better: it would
1444	leave a prompt on screen that nobody is waiting on, and answer "no store
1445	available" for a machine that has a perfectly good one — sending the user to the
1446	memory fallback because their keyring was locked. Every other client of the
1447	Secret Service behaves the same way, including git's own `libsecret` helper. The
1448	prompt is the user's keyring policy working; suppressing it is not DevDesk's
1449	call to make.
1450	
1451	Windows and macOS have no equivalent: `CredRead` is silent for the current user,
1452	and `security find-generic-password` only prompts for items the calling binary
1453	is not on the ACL of — which, for items DevDesk itself wrote, it is.
1454	
1455	---
1456	
1457	### 3.10 An inference-backed explainer for network diagnostics
1458	
1459	Netdiag runs the tests but leaves the interpretation to the user. The first —
1460	and for now only — AI feature is an **explainer over diagnostic results that
1461	DevDesk already holds**. It sends a few kilobytes of structured facts, needs no
1462	new privilege, and touches no packet payload.
1463	
1464	#### Settled
1465	
1466	| # | Question | Decision |
1467	|---|---|---|
1468	| 1 | Scope of v1 | **Explainer only.** No capture. tcpdump is a later input to the same explainer, not part of this. |
1469	| 2 | Local server lifecycle | **DevDesk consumes an endpoint.** It never starts, stops or supervises an inference server. |
1470	| 3 | Protocol | **One OpenAI-compatible client** (`POST /v1/chat/completions`). Covers ollama, llama.cpp, vLLM, LM Studio and hosted providers. No second native client. |
1471	| 4 | Redaction | **Nothing sensitive reaches a model, local or remote.** Not a per-provider policy — one rule, no exception for `localhost`. |
1472	| 5 | Snaplen | Headers-only is the default **when capture arrives**. Out of scope for v1 by decision 1. |
1473	| 6 | Provider scope | **One per context.** |
1474	
1475	Decisions 2 and 6 cost nothing. Consuming an endpoint means the provider is a
1476	URL, a model name and a token — a `AIConfig` block in the context's
1477	`config.yaml`, which is per-context by construction. The token goes to the store
1478	from §3.9 like any other; it must never land in the YAML. The GPU question that
1479	motivated hosting (Docker on macOS runs a Linux VM with no Metal access, so
1480	unified memory is unreachable from a container) disappears with it: the user
1481	runs `ollama serve` natively, or a container, or nothing, and DevDesk does not
1482	care.
1483	
1484	#### The hard part is decision 4, and Presidio only half-answers it
1485	
1486	Reference: [Docker agent PII protection with
1487	Presidio](https://k33g.org/p/20260716-docker-agent-pii-protection-presidio) —
1488	an analyzer/anonymizer pair behind HTTP, hooked on `before_llm_call`, replacing
1489	detected spans with typed tokens.
1490	
1491	Two things transfer and one does not.
1492	
1493	**What does not transfer: the entity set.** Presidio detects *PII* — names,
1494	emails, phone numbers, credit cards, IBANs, national IDs, IP addresses. What
1495	DevDesk holds is mostly not PII: internal hostnames, private ranges, resolver
1496	addresses, listening sockets and process names, registry and forge URLs,
1497	Gitleaks matches. `IP_ADDRESS` is the only real overlap. A DevDesk payload could
1498	pass Presidio clean while still describing the whole internal network. Presidio
1499	is therefore a **second net, not the mechanism**.
1500	
1501	**What transfers: fail-closed, and the deterministic layers.** The post notes
1502	its own default is fail-open and that production needs `PII_FAIL_CLOSED=1`.
1503	Given §3.9, fail-closed is the only acceptable mode here: if the redactor is
1504	unreachable, nothing is sent, and the user is told why. And the post's two
1505	non-NER layers — a deny-list and structural rules by column — are the parts
1506	that actually caught things reliably. That is the direction to build in.
1507	
1508	#### Allow-list construction beats scrubbing
1509	
1510	The post scrubs because it hooks arbitrary agent traffic and cannot know what is
1511	in it. DevDesk is not in that position: it **assembles the payload itself** from
1512	`m.results`, which is already typed and structured. So the payload should be
1513	built field by field from an explicit allow-list, not produced as a blob and
1514	then cleaned.
1515	
1516	The difference matters: **a field never included cannot fail to be redacted.**
1517	Scrubbing is a filter that can miss; construction is a whitelist that cannot.
1518	Presidio then runs over the assembled payload as a check on the construction,
1519	and any hit is a bug in the allow-list, not a routine save.
1520	
1521	#### The tension: the sensitive data *is* the diagnostic data
1522	
1523	Redacting addresses out of a network diagnostic destroys the diagnostic. A model
1524	told `[IP_REDACTED]` resolves to `[IP_REDACTED]` can conclude nothing, and the
1525	answer that comes back is unreadable.
1526	
1527	The resolution is **consistent pseudonymisation that preserves the analytically
1528	relevant class**, not blanket redaction:
1529	
1530	| Real | Sent | Preserved |
1531	|---|---|---|
1532	| `api.corp.internal` | `host-1` | identity across the payload |
1533	| `10.2.3.4` | `private-a` | RFC1918, and same-subnet relations |
1534	| `203.0.113.9` | `public-b` | routable, distinct from private |
1535	| `10.2.3.7` | `private-c` | same /24 as `private-a` |
1536	
1537	The hypotheses the model is asked to rank depend on structure — private vs
1538	public, same subnet or not, resolves or not, port open or filtered, which TLS
1539	stage failed — never on the literal octets. So this loses nothing. "host-1
1540	resolves to private-a but hop 5 is public-c, so the route leaves your network"
1541	is exactly as useful as the version with real addresses.
1542	
1543	The mapping stays in memory, and the response is **restored locally before
1544	display**, so the user reads real names. The blog post does not do this
1545	round-trip — its tokens are one-way — but DevDesk needs it, because unlike a
1546	CSV of customers its payload is *entirely* made of identifiers.
1547	
1548	#### Confirmation before send
1549	
1550	The assembled, pseudonymised payload is rendered in the viewport before it
1551	leaves, for every provider. Decision 4 says local and remote are treated alike,
1552	so there is no "trusted endpoint" shortcut. This costs one keypress and is what
1553	makes the feature auditable without reading the source.
1554	
1555	#### Bubble Tea shape
1556	
1557	Streaming is the only delicate part. Rule 110 forbids mutating the model inside
1558	a `Cmd`, so the pattern is a channel plus a `Cmd` that reads one chunk and
1559	returns a `streamChunkMsg{gen, text}` which re-arms itself — the same shape as
1560	the spinner, reusing the generation counter already in `run.go:33` to discard a
1561	superseded stream.
1562	
1563	Cancellation is mandatory, not optional: a local model on CPU can take minutes.
1564	A `context.CancelFunc` lives in the model and `esc` cancels. **D13 is the
1565	warning** — a state the user cannot leave while something resolves is a defect
1566	this repository already has once.
1567	
1568	No new view and no command. The explanation is a results tab under the table
1569	(Rule 123), triggered by a key on the results screen. A dedicated view turns
1570	this into a chat product, which is not what is being asked for. With no provider
1571	configured the shortcut is absent rather than erroring (Rule 130), and all
1572	strings are English US (Rule 129).
1573	
1574	#### Sketch of the work
1575	
1576	1. `internal/ai`: config block, an OpenAI-compatible client behind a small
1577	   interface so tests inject a fake — the `runner` indirection in
1578	   `internal/docker` is the precedent — and the token read from the §3.9 store.
1579	2. The payload builder: allow-listed fields out of `m.results`, plus the
1580	   pseudonymiser and its inverse. Table-driven tests, like the existing
1581	   `dns_formatter` and `traceroute_formatter` parsers. **This is the feature; do
1582	   it first and it is testable with no endpoint at all.**
1583	3. The prompt: observed facts only, and an instruction to name which test each
1584	   claim rests on. The raw results stay on screen next to the explanation —
1585	   the narrative never replaces the data.
1586	4. Streaming, cancellation, and the results tab.
1587	5. The confirmation pane.
1588	6. Optional and last: Presidio as a fail-closed second net over the assembled
1589	   payload, behind a config flag. Two containers and a spaCy model is heavy
1590	   for a few kilobytes of already-structured text, and step 2 is what actually
1591	   provides the guarantee.
1592	
1593	Later, and explicitly not now: capture as an additional input (bounded by `-c`
1594	and `-G`, `-s 96` by default so payloads cannot be captured at all), and the
1595	deterministic flow summariser that would have to precede it — a pcap does not
1596	fit in a context window, and once the summariser exists it answers most of the
1597	question without a model. `nicolaka/netshoot` (`config.go:218`) already ships
1598	`tcpdump` and `tshark`, and the privileged host-namespace runner exists
1599	(`ports.go:36`, `topology.go:47`), so the missing piece is the analysis, not the
1600	plumbing.
1601	
1602	Adjacent candidates, ranked, none settled: Trivy remediation (§3.2 — low
1603	sensitivity, but any suggested base-image bump must be verified by a re-scan,
1604	never trusted); Gitleaks triage (highest value since false positives dominate,
1605	highest risk since the payload *is* the secret — possibly viable by sending rule
1606	name, path and entropy with the match withheld); container log explanation
1607	(logs carry env vars and DSNs routinely).
1608	
1609	---

content.text:
## Prochaine étape : §2 phase 6 — couverture de tests

C'est le seul item marqué `pending` dans le plan de couverture, et c'est aussi ce qui débloque §3.8 (qui porte D12–D14, les trois seuls défauts encore ouverts). §3.8 dit explicitement : *surface tests → split → couverture → puis la feature*. Le split de `oci_resources` est fait (phase 4), la couverture ne l'est pas.

### État réel mesuré à l'instant

Total **73.8 %** (le backlog dit 73.6 %, légèrement périmé — quelques packages ont bougé avec §3.9 : `app` 91.1, `auth` 97.2, `status` 94.6). Pour atteindre 80 % il faut couvrir **~705 statements** sur les ~2 900 non couverts.

| Package | Non couverts | % |
|---|---|---|
| `internal/ui/oci_resources` | **1 509** | 43.4 |
| `internal/docker` | 205 | 65.4 |
| `internal/registrymgr` | 75 | 18.5 |
| `internal/oci` | 74 | 37.3 |
| `internal/status` | 69 | 64.8 |
| `internal/cache` | 50 | 71.3 |
| `internal/ui/terminal` | 52 | 0.0 |

`oci_resources` domine à lui seul : en couvrir la moitié suffit à passer la barre. Et le détail par fichier confirme ce que le backlog avait anticipé — ce qui reste, c'est exactement ce qui attendait le seam de la phase 5, **qui existe maintenant** (`dockerRunner`) :

| Fichier | Non couverts | % |
|---|---|---|
| `commands.go` (chaque invocation `docker`) | 256 | 6.9 |
| `connectivity_form.go` | 196 | 0.0 |
| `launch_form.go` | 136 | 34.0 |
| `browser_keys.go` | 117 | 8.6 |
| `browser_view.go` | 100 | 1.0 |
| `browser_tags.go` | 90 | 3.2 |

`commands.go` + les trois fichiers `browser_*` = 563 statements, et ce sont précisément les chemins que §3.8 réécrit — donc les tests écrits là servent deux fois.

### Découpage proposé

1. **PR 6a — `oci_resources`** : `commands.go` via `dockerRunner`, puis `browser_*` et les formulaires. C'est ce qui fait basculer le total au-dessus de 80 %.
2. **PR 6b — le reste** : `registrymgr` (18.5 %, et `CanHandle` change en §3.8 étape 4), `oci` (il manque le fixture `httptest` manifest + layer gzippé), `status` et `docker` (les deux ont un seam et « aucune excuse », dixit le backlog), `cache`.

Ensuite seulement §3.8 (avec D12–D14 en tests inversés d'abord), ou §3.10 étape 2 (le payload builder + pseudonymiseur, testable sans endpoint) si tu préfères une feature.

Je démarre sur 6a — `commands.go` en premier ?
oui

151	func (f *ConnectivityTestForm) SetResult(output string, err error) {
152		f.state = connectivityStateResults

154		f.resultScroll = 0
155		if err != nil {

157			errMsg := strings.TrimPrefix(err.Error(), "diagnostic command failed: ")
158			f.resultErr = errMsg
159			// If there is output, the container ran but exited non-zero (e.g. curl/nc exit codes)

168	func (f *ConnectivityTestForm) Update(msg tea.Msg) (*ConnectivityTestForm, tea.Cmd) {

171			return f, nil
172		}
173	
174		// Results state: scroll with ↑/↓, enter resets to input
175		if f.state == connectivityStateResults {
176			if key, ok := msg.(tea.KeyMsg); ok {
177				resultLines := strings.Split(f.result, "\n")
178				visibleLines := f.resultVisibleLines()
179				switch key.String() {
180				case "enter":
181					f.state = connectivityStateInput
182					f.result = ""
183					f.resultErr = ""
184					f.resultExitCode = false
185					f.resultScroll = 0
186				case "up", "k":
187					if f.resultScroll > 0 {

189					}

194					}
195				case "g", "home":

197				case "G", "end":

202		}

204		switch msg := msg.(type) {

210					if f.containerListIdx > 0 {

212					} else {

214					}

228					f.containerListIdx++

232				// Otherwise: navigate to next field (Rule 135)

242					if !f.isPortActive() && f.focusedField >= f.numFields() {

253					if !f.isPortActive() && f.focusedField >= f.numFields() {
254						f.focusedField = f.numFields() - 1
255					}
256					f.updateFocus()
257				}
258				return f, nil
259	
260			case "enter":
261				if f.focusedField == f.submitIdx() {
262					target := strings.TrimSpace(f.targetInput.Value())
263					if target == "" {

365	func (f *ConnectivityTestForm) renderSuggestions(w int) []string {
366		lines := make([]string, 0, len(f.containers)+1)
367		// Section header
368		lines = append(lines, theme.PadWithBg(theme.DimStyle.Render("    Containers on this network:"), w))
369		for i, c := range f.containers {
370			name := c.Name
371			ip := c.IPv4
372			if ip == "" {
373				ip = "—"
374			}
375			selected := i == f.containerListIdx
376			// Name padded to align IP column
377			namePadded := name
378			if len(namePadded) < 24 {
379				namePadded += strings.Repeat(" ", 24-len(namePadded))
380			}
381			entry := namePadded + "  " + ip
382			var line string
383			if selected {

385					lipgloss.NewStyle().Background(theme.ColorBackground).Foreground(theme.ColorHighlight).Bold(true).Render("    "+theme.IconCircleSmall+" "+entry),
386					w,
387				)
388			} else {

390			}

396	// resultVisibleLines returns how many output lines fit in the viewport.
397	// Header (3) + status (1) + empty (1) + empty (1) = 6 fixed lines (no inline help per Rule 134).
398	func (f *ConnectivityTestForm) resultVisibleLines() int {
399		return max(f.height-6, 3)
400	}

402	// truncateResultLine truncates a plain-text line to maxRunes visible characters,
403	// appending "…" when truncation occurs. CLI output has no ANSI codes, so rune
404	// counting is sufficient and safe.
405	func truncateResultLine(s string, maxRunes int) string {
406		if maxRunes <= 0 {
407			return ""
408		}
409		runes := []rune(s)
410		if len(runes) <= maxRunes {
411			return s
412		}
413		return string(runes[:maxRunes-1]) + "…"
414	}

416	func (f *ConnectivityTestForm) renderResults(w int) []string {
417		var lines []string
418	
419		// Status header
420		switch {
421		case f.resultErr != "" && !f.resultExitCode:
422			// Hard failure: no output, only error
423			lines = append(lines, theme.PadWithBg(theme.StatusErrorStyle.Render("  "+theme.IconError+" "+f.resultErr), w))
424		case f.resultErr != "" && f.resultExitCode:
425			// Non-zero exit but output present (e.g. curl exit 52, nc exit 1)
426			warnStyle := lipgloss.NewStyle().Background(theme.ColorBackground).Foreground(theme.ColorWarn)
427			lines = append(lines, theme.PadWithBg(warnStyle.Render("  "+theme.IconWarning+" "+f.resultErr), w))
428		default:
429			okStyle := lipgloss.NewStyle().Background(theme.ColorBackground).Foreground(theme.ColorOK)
430			lines = append(lines, theme.PadWithBg(okStyle.Render("  "+theme.IconOK+" Test completed"), w))
431		}
432		lines = append(lines, theme.EmptyLineBg(w))
433	
434		// Scrollable output
435		if f.result != "" {
436			allLines := strings.Split(f.result, "\n")
437			visible := f.resultVisibleLines()
438			end := min(f.resultScroll+visible, len(allLines))
439			maxContent := w - 3 // 2 indent + 1 for "…"
440			for _, line := range allLines[f.resultScroll:end] {
441				line = strings.TrimRight(line, "\r") // strip Windows-style CR
442				line = truncateResultLine(line, maxContent)
443				lines = append(lines, theme.PadWithBg(theme.Bg("  "+line), w))
444			}
445			// Scroll indicator when content overflows
446			if len(allLines) > visible {
447				indicator := theme.DimStyle.Render(
448					fmt.Sprintf("  [%d–%d / %d lines]", f.resultScroll+1, end, len(allLines)),
449				)
450				lines = append(lines, theme.PadWithBg(indicator, w))
451			}
452		}
453	
454		lines = append(lines, theme.EmptyLineBg(w))
455		return lines
456	}

90	// newRegistryBrowser creates a RegistryBrowser and fires group-detection commands for all
91	// configured registries. The browser starts in browserStateResolving until all detections
92	// complete; it then transitions to browserStateInput with the resolved entry list.
93	func newRegistryBrowser(registries []config.RegistryItem, width, height int) (*RegistryBrowser, tea.Cmd) {
94		repoInput := textinput.New()
95		repoInput.Placeholder = "nginx  (or library/nginx)"
96		repoInput.CharLimit = 256
97		theme.StyleTextInput(&repoInput)
98		repoInput.Focus()

100		fi := textinput.New()

105		tagCols := []table.Column{

107			{Title: "Tag", Width: 30},
108			{Title: "Updated", Width: 16},
109			{Title: "C", Width: 4},
110			{Title: "H", Width: 4},
111			{Title: "M", Width: 4},
112			{Title: "L", Width: 4},
113		}
114		tt := table.New(
115			table.WithColumns(tagCols),
116			table.WithFocused(true),
117			table.WithHeight(10),
118		)
119		tt.SetStyles(theme.DefaultTableStyles())
120	
121		sp := spinner.New()
122		sp.Spinner = spinner.Dot
123		sp.Style = theme.SpinnerStyle()
124	
125		b := &RegistryBrowser{
126			registries:        registries,
127			entryGroups:       make([][]browserRegistryEntry, len(registries)),
128			pendingDetections: len(registries),
129			width:             width,
130			height:            height,
131			repoInput:         repoInput,
132			selectedRegs:      make(map[string]bool),
133			focusedField:      brFieldRepo,
134			filterInput:       fi,
135			tagSortCol:        tagSortByName,
136			tagSortDesc:       false,
137			tagTable:          tt,
138			spinner:           sp,
139			scanCache:         make(map[string]cache.ImageScanEntry),
140			scanningTags:      make(map[string]bool),
141			state:             browserStateResolving,
142		}
143		b.resizeInputs()
144		b.resizeTagTable()

146		if len(registries) == 0 {

148			return b, nil
149		}

151		cmds := make([]tea.Cmd, 0, len(registries)+1)
152		for _, reg := range registries {

167	// HandleGroupDetected incorporates one detection result into the ordered entry list.
168	// When all detections have completed it finalizes entries and switches to input state.
169	func (b *RegistryBrowser) HandleGroupDetected(msg RegistryGroupDetectedMsg) (*RegistryBrowser, tea.Cmd) {
170		for i, reg := range b.registries {
171			if reg.URL != msg.RegistryURL {
172				continue
173			}
174			alias := reg.Alias
175			if alias == "" {
176				alias = reg.URL
177			}
178			if len(msg.Members) > 0 {
179				group := make([]browserRegistryEntry, len(msg.Members))
180				for j, m := range msg.Members {
181					group[j] = browserRegistryEntry{
182						URL:         m.URL,
183						Alias:       m.Alias,
184						ParentAlias: alias,
185						parentURL:   reg.URL,
186					}
187				}
188				b.entryGroups[i] = group
189			} else {
190				b.entryGroups[i] = []browserRegistryEntry{{URL: reg.URL, Alias: alias}}
191			}
192			break
193		}
194		b.pendingDetections--
195		if b.pendingDetections <= 0 {
196			b.finalizeEntries()
197		}
198		return b, nil
199	}
200	
201	// finalizeEntries flattens entryGroups into entries, initialises selectedRegs (all checked),
202	// and transitions the browser to the input form state.
203	func (b *RegistryBrowser) finalizeEntries() {
204		b.entries = nil
205		for _, group := range b.entryGroups {
206			b.entries = append(b.entries, group...)
207		}
208		b.selectedRegs = make(map[string]bool, len(b.entries))
209		for _, e := range b.entries {
210			b.selectedRegs[e.URL] = true
211		}
212		b.state = browserStateInput
213		b.updateFocus()
214	}
215	
216	func (b *RegistryBrowser) resizeInputs() {
217		w := max(b.width-22, 20)
218		b.repoInput.Width = w
219		b.filterInput.Width = max(b.width-6, 10)
220	}
221	
222	func (b *RegistryBrowser) resizeTagTable() {
223		b.tagTable.SetHeight(max(b.height, 1))
224	
225		// b.width is already the viewport content width (full width - 2 borders).
226		// Subtract only the cell padding (numCols × 2) so column widths sum exactly to `available`.
227		const numCols = 7
228		available := max(b.width-numCols*2, 10)
229		fixedReg := 20
230		fixedUpdated := 16
231		fixedC, fixedH, fixedM := 4, 4, 4
232		fixedSum := fixedReg + fixedUpdated + fixedC + fixedH + fixedM
233		flexTag := max(available-fixedSum-4, 8) // reserve 4 for last col minimum
234	
235		cols := b.tagTable.Columns()
236		if len(cols) == numCols {
237			cols[0].Width = fixedReg
238			cols[1].Width = flexTag
239			cols[2].Width = fixedUpdated
240			cols[3].Width = fixedC
241			cols[4].Width = fixedH
242			cols[5].Width = fixedM
243			// Last column absorbs leftover so sum(col_widths) == available exactly.
244			cols[6].Width = available - fixedReg - flexTag - fixedUpdated - fixedC - fixedH - fixedM
245			b.tagTable.SetColumns(cols)
246		}
247	
248		// Force the Selected row style to span the viewport content width so the selected
249		// background extends to the right border, even when row content visually differs
250		// from the calculated width (e.g. Nerd Font icon width discrepancies). See workspaces fix.
251		styles := theme.DefaultTableStyles()
252		styles.Selected = styles.Selected.Width(b.width)
253		b.tagTable.SetStyles(styles)
254	}
